searchText: I guess you missed some attestations I'm not counting those towards bad head vote Those are due to a different phenomenon This is a known issue with Eth2 presently. I’ve spoken about it in this channel, I link to it afterwards. Basically block propagation is (unnecessarily IMO) slow at the moment which is causing blocks to arrive after attestations are sent out. An oversight in the Eth2 spec means that these late blocks don’t get attested to but they still end up in the chain, causing a missed head vote. (Oh I thought I was in LH discord) Here’s my post in LH discord. https://discord.com/channels/605577013327167508/605577013331361793/805678894078361611 LH release with faster propagation is scheduled for next week. If you attest on the first slot of an epoch, your head vote is identical to the target vote. You’d expect target misses to be ~1/32rd of head vote misses, but perhaps there’s additional factors. I’m unsure as to why source votes would miss. Right. I'm interested in why the last 7 days are considerably worse than the last 30 days To potuz's point, could be under resourced machines I think it's still considerably more than 1/32, even with all optimizations we are seeing more blocks arriving late on slot 0 and some clients have still more bottlenecks executing epoch transition before syncing the new head block But indeed this problem has grown considerably worse these last few weeks. To the point that the misses in slot 0 are irrelevant when they used to be the only ones Hi everyone, would you know some open source software I could run to obtain an address for the withdrawal key the same way it is displayed on a Ledger X? Do you want it from the Ledger, or from a mnemonic you would supply?

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
This is a known issue with Eth2 presently. I’ve spoken about it in this channel, I link to it afterwards.

Basically block propagation is (unnecessarily IMO) slow at the moment which is causing blocks to arrive after attestations are sent out. 

An oversight in the Eth2 spec means that these late blocks don’t get attested to but they still end up in the chain, causing a missed head vote.

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
If you attest on the first slot of an epoch, your head vote is identical to the target vote. You’d expect target misses to be ~1/32rd of head vote misses, but perhaps there’s additional factors. 

I’m unsure as to why source votes would miss.

excerpts.content: I think it's still considerably more than 1/32, even with all optimizations we are seeing more blocks arriving late on slot 0 and some clients have still more bottlenecks executing epoch transition before syncing the new head block

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: But indeed this problem has grown considerably worse these last few weeks. To the point that the misses in slot 0 are irrelevant when they used to be the only ones
